mentor_context.message: Use the three-burden proof ladder for every new learned distinction: B1 abstraction, B2 causal use, B3 internalization. Do not promote a distinction because its state is readable or its outputs look compliant. First require held-out recombination/opaque-renaming or equivalent controls that defeat surface retrieval; then prefreeze downstream metrics and use ablation plus targeted intervention to prove the distinction changes later cognition/action; only then test internalization with capability-specific source removal, restart/rehydration, delayed reuse, decoy cues, fresh transfer, and independent/evaluator-hidden return. The learner's self-report has zero promotion weight. Preserve WITHHOLD when any burden is missing. Apply dependency-DAG scheduling to this evidence ladder: parallelize independent probes, but do not spend B3 work before B1/B2 are earned. For the current #78 semantic-trace episode, treat the prefrozen lexical-vs-relation comparator as B1/B2 evidence only unless the stronger B3 conditions are separately met. Keep mentor hints below returned defects and learner-owned problem formation, and fade the mentor as she learns to generate her own discriminators and anti-shortcut controls.

returned_blocker_sentences: Where learner ownership is itself under test, the candidate must be frozen before hidden evaluator exposure.
A hidden test improves confidence in evaluation integrity; it does not establish generality outside the tested distribution.

It pins exact learner-state and generic-executor Git blobs, requires post-commit hidden examples, keeps gold/scoring outside candidate execution, prohibits post-exposure patches, and retains PASS/FAIL/WITHHOLD/INVALID dispositions.
